AllowedRetentionPolicy.title: AllowedRetentionPolicy

AutumnPlanMetadata.description:
Typed view of an Autumn plan's ``metadata`` object.

The full contract, as configured on the plan in the Autumn dashboard::

    {
      "rate_limit_per_minute": 25,
      "retention_policy": {
        "allowed_retention_policy": {
          "period": [7, 30, 90, 365, null],
          "scope": ["transcript_recording", "caller_data", "full"]
        },
        "default_retention_policy": {"period": 30, "scope": "caller_data"}
      }
    }

This model is **intentionally permissive** because plan metadata is untrusted external
input consumed on paths that must not fail hard (the settings API and the Autumn webhook
reconciler). Unrelated metadata keys are ignored, every sub-object defaults to an empty
instance so any level may be absent, and non-dict/non-list values fail closed to those
empty defaults with a warning instead of raising. Use :meth:`parse_safe` rather than
``model_validate`` so a wholly wrong payload cannot raise either.

``rate_limit_per_minute`` being **absent** is meaningfully different from it being
**null**: absent means "this plan says nothing about rate limiting, leave the workspace
alone", null means "unlimited". ``None`` alone cannot express that, so callers MUST use
``"rate_limit_per_minute" in plan.model_fields_set`` to tell the two apart.

Attributes:
    rate_limit_per_minute: The plan's per-minute request cap; ``None`` means unlimited.
        Check ``model_fields_set`` before trusting ``None`` -- see above.
    retention_policy: The data-retention contract. Empty when absent or malformed.
AutumnPlanMetadata.title: AutumnPlanMetadata

PlanSummary.description:
A single plan entry returned by GET /plans.

A reasonably complete passthrough of ``autumn_sdk.models.Plan``'s pricing
fields (mirroring ``CustomerResponse`` below): the frontend needs ``price``
and ``items`` to render dollar amounts, per-plan feature checklists, and
per-cycle credit counts, none of which can be derived from
``id``/``name``/``add_on`` alone.

``metadata`` is the plan's dashboard-authored metadata, already returned inline
by Autumn's ``plans.list`` (no per-plan ``plans.get`` fetch needed). It is typed
as :class:`AutumnPlanMetadata` so the documented contract
(``rate_limit_per_minute`` / ``retention_policy``) is the shape clients code
against, and falls back to the raw dict when the payload does not fit that
structure at all -- see ``_map_plan_metadata`` in the endpoint module. A plan with
no metadata serializes the same nested skeleton with empty values rather than a bare
``{}``, so the shape does not vary from plan to plan within one response.

Note that ``rate_limit_per_minute`` serializes as ``null`` both when the plan
omits it and when it explicitly sets it to null; the absent-vs-null distinction
that ``model_fields_set`` preserves server-side does not survive to the wire.
Only the webhook reconciler depends on that distinction, and it reads plan
metadata directly rather than through this response.

RuleCreate.description:
Schema for creating a rule.

Describe the condition with `condition_tree`.

condition_tree.description: The condition a call must match. The root is always a group (`AND` or `OR`) of predicates and nested groups, even for a single condition, and every node needs a `type` (`group` or `predicate`). Build each predicate from an item in List Rule Conditions: for an eval, a data extraction field or a voice metric, `lhs` is the item's name, `source` its `source_type` and `field_id` its `id`; for a latency percentile, `lhs` is the item's `id` (such as `"p90_latency"`); for Call Outcome, Call Intent, Call Duration, Call Cost, Call Outcome Type and Call Ended Reason, `lhs` is `call_outcome`, `call_intent`, `call_duration`, `call_cost`, `call_outcome_type` or `call_ended_reason`; for Extra Metadata, `lhs` is `metadata.<key>`. `op` is a word (`eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `exists`, `not_exists`, `contains`, `starts_with`), not the symbol List Rule Conditions returns. `eq`, `neq`, `contains` and `starts_with` on text ignore case. `exists` and `not_exists` work on any field, even where List Rule Conditions doesn't list them. A field with no value for the call counts as not existing. A field the analysis skipped, such as an eval that didn't run or the intent of a call whose outcome stopped the analysis, matches only `not_exists`, not even `neq`. Groups nest at most 10 levels deep, and a tree holds at most 50 conditions.

put.description:
Set a workspace's data-retention window and erasure scope.

Expired calls are erased by a nightly job, so a change takes effect on its next run.
**Erasure is irreversible**: an erased call cannot be restored. Simulation calls are never
erased.
